lincoln-national-park-3.name: Cape Donington
lincoln-national-park-3.bio: A headland on the south-east coast of Lincoln National Park with a lighthouse and views to Donington Island.

notes.pin: Wikipedia point (34.733,136.0) is a rounded region point, not the headland: pin the Cape Donington Lighthouse / lookout feature (OSM man_made=lighthouse) instead. Not named on the NPWS park page.
notes.cost: Lincoln NP vehicle entry $14.40 per vehicle (parks.sa.gov.au/parks/lincoln-national-park, fees box); applies if reached through the park.

lincoln-national-park-4.name: Sleaford Bay
lincoln-national-park-4.bio: A surf beach in Lincoln National Park, with lookouts for southern right whales between May and October.

notes.pin: Wikipedia point is the bay centroid (likely in water). Use the Wanna Lookout / Lone Pine Lookout (NPWS: most accessible whale spotting) or the beach access car park.
notes.cost: Lincoln NP vehicle entry $14.40 per vehicle, same park fee.

coffin-bay-1.name: Coffin Bay National Park
coffin-bay-1.bio: Coastal park of high cliffs, big dunes, surf beaches and sheltered bays west of Coffin Bay, with 4WD tracks north.

notes.pin: Wikipedia point is a park centroid. Use a visitor point: the park entrance/information bay off Coffin Bay town road, or Yangie Bay / Point Avoid car park (different from Yangie Bay spot pin).
notes.cost: Vehicle entry $14.40 per vehicle (parks.sa.gov.au coffin-bay-national-park, fees box).

coffin-bay-2.name: Coffin Bay Oyster Walk
coffin-bay-2.bio: An 8 km signposted shoreline walk from Long Beach to Snapper Point, past the boat ramp, jetty and oyster waters.
coffin-bay-2.ticket_note: Walk along the town foreshore; only the regional tourism page describes it, no single steward site found.

notes.pin: Pin at midpoint of the 8 km route (OSM route Coffin Bay Oyster Walk, Long Beach to Snapper Point). Optional loop via Kellidie Bay Conservation Park lookout.
notes.cost: No fee mentioned on the regional tourism page; open foreshore track.

coffin-bay-3.name: Yangie Bay
coffin-bay-3.bio: A bay at the south end of Coffin Bay National Park, reached by 2WD, for canoeing, picnics and a coastal bushwalk.

notes.pin: Yangie Bay day-use / picnic area and boat launch car park (OSM), inside the park on the bay shore.
notes.wiki: Check a Yangie Bay Wikipedia article exists; draft carries wiki Yangie Bay, drop if it redirects or is absent.

coffin-bay-4.name: Almonta Beach
coffin-bay-4.bio: A surf beach on the Coffin Bay National Park coast, partly reached by 4WD, with fishing along the sand.

notes.pin: Almonta Beach access / car park or beach feature (OSM natural=beach) on the park coast; NPWS lists fishing on Gunya and Almonta Beach.
notes.wiki: Check a Wikipedia article exists; drop wiki if not.

streaky-bay-1.name: Murphy's Haystacks
streaky-bay-1.bio: Pink granite inselbergs rising from farmland near Streaky Bay, with a picnic area, toilets and a campground.
streaky-bay-1.ticket_note: Privately owned farm site; no official website found on the regional tourism page.

notes.pin: Wikipedia point (-33.015194, 134.4887972) names the formation; confirm against the site entrance/car park.
notes.cost: Entry is on private property and a donation is appreciated for the picnic area and toilets (regional tourism page).

streaky-bay-2.name: Cape Bauer Loop
streaky-bay-2.bio: A coastal drive to Cape Bauer on the Great Australian Bight, with Hallys Beach lookout, blowholes and views of Olive Island.
streaky-bay-2.ticket_note: Public road; no single steward site.

notes.pin: Loop of Cape Bauer Road / Stanley Williams Road; pin at the Cape Bauer Lookout or the loop midpoint, not the same as Whistling Rocks.

streaky-bay-3.name: Whistling Rocks and the Blowholes
streaky-bay-3.bio: Whistling rocks and blowholes on Cape Bauer, reached by a 360 m boardwalk to cliff platforms, best at high tide.
streaky-bay-3.ticket_note: Public site on the Cape Bauer Loop; no single steward site.

notes.pin: End of the 360 m boardwalk / viewing platforms on Cape Bauer Loop; at least 25 m from the Cape Bauer Loop pin.

streaky-bay-4.name: Westall Way Loop
streaky-bay-4.bio: A 32 km unsealed scenic loop passing Smooth Pool, High Cliffs, The Granites and Cape Bauer Lookout.
streaky-bay-4.ticket_note: Public road; no single steward site.

notes.pin: Loop begins from Sceale Bay Road; pin at the loop midpoint (e.g. High Cliffs or The Granites), not at Cape Bauer Lookout used by the Cape Bauer Loop.

destination.name: Coffin Bay
destination.tagline: An oyster-farming village on a calm bay, beside a wild coastal national park.
destination.description: Coffin Bay is a small village on the western side of the Eyre Peninsula, about 40 minutes' drive from Port Lincoln. Matthew Flinders named the bay after his friend Sir Isaac Coffin, and the town is known for its oysters. Coffin Bay National Park to the west has windswept cliffs, dunes, surf beaches and sheltered bays, and Kellidie Bay Conservation Park lies to the east. An 8 km foreshore trail follows the shore past the jetty and the oyster-growing waters.
whyVisit: Taste oysters fresh from the bay
Explore a wild coastal national park

goodToKnow.title: Know your 4WD access
goodToKnow.detail: The park's northern beaches need a high-clearance 4WD, while Yangie Bay and Point Avoid can be reached in a 2WD.

goodToKnow.title: Pay park entry first
goodToKnow.detail: Vehicle entry to Coffin Bay National Park is $14.40 and must be paid before you go in.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are the warm months for swimming, boating and fishing on the bay, and the village is busiest then.

destination.name: Streaky Bay
destination.tagline: A west-coast fishing town with blowholes, sea cliffs and granite haystacks nearby.
destination.description: Streaky Bay is a fishing and farming town on the west side of the Eyre Peninsula, 303 km north-west of Port Lincoln. Matthew Flinders named the bay in 1802 for the streaks of discoloured water he saw. A 350 m jetty runs out from the town centre and oysters and abalone are farmed in the bay. Coastal loops lead to blowholes and cliffs at Cape Bauer, and Murphy's Haystacks stand on farmland to the south-east.

goodToKnow.title: Time the blowholes
goodToKnow.detail: Whistling Rocks and the Blowholes are most active at high tide with a big swell.

goodToKnow.title: Unsealed loop roads
goodToKnow.detail: The Westall Way Loop is unsealed and has rough sections, so drive with care.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} suit swimming off the jetty and long drives along the coastal loops.
